::: {.callout-tip}
## One coherent example

We use six invented shop orders with **distance (km)**, **number of items**, and **fulfilment time (minutes)**. Start the [single-file Python example](../../examples/README.md); this chapter corresponds to `python3 delivery_ml_lab.py pca`.
:::

## The motivating problem

**How can we compress features without knowing a label?**

PCA chooses orthogonal directions that retain variance, and equivalently minimise reconstruction error. Eigendecomposition, SVD and low-rank approximation are different views of the same geometric operation for centred Euclidean data.

## Central mathematical relationship

$$
\max_{\|w\|_2=1} w^\top Sw=\lambda_{\max}(S)
$$

The equation captures the chapter's principal relationship. Definitions and assumptions are developed in the lessons below; an equation is useful only when the domain and meaning of its symbols are explicit.

## First worked result

The two order features have sample covariance approximately [[3.5,1.2],[1.2,0.8]]. The dominant eigenvector gives a one-number representation emphasising a direction mostly aligned with distance.

## What to pay attention to

Retaining variance is not identical to retaining label relevance. Scale on training data only and evaluate the effect on the downstream task.

Read the lessons in sequence, reproduce a calculation by hand, then run the related Python demonstration and explain which mathematical claim the output illustrates. A numerical observation is never, by itself, proof of a theorem.
